newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends firmer, sluggish trading seen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends firmer, sluggish trading seen.

text.p: The won closed higher on Thursday as some banks went short on the dollar, and dealers said the market would drift sideways for the time being.
They said domestic companies were the major players in the recent won/dollar market, while bank dealers remained cautious as they differed over the future direction.
The won ended at 893.70, compared with the close of 893.90 on Wednesday. After opening at 893.50, the won rose to 892.50.
But the won fell to 894.20 on fears of a central bank intervention and on looming importer deals at the weekend.
Dealers forecast an expected inflow of foreign funds to invest in the local stock market would depress the dollar.
"The dollar will move below the 895.00 won level," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said trading volume amounted to $1.18 billion on Thursday. Friday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 893.40 from 894.30.
